services.name: NY Connects
services.desc: In Brooklyn, PSS runs NY Connects for NYC Aging. Staff give free, unbiased help with long-term care choices, check eligibility for benefits, help with applications and refer families to home care. Call 718-671-6200.

services.name: Case management and home delivered meals
services.desc: A local case management agency does a phone intake, then a case manager visits the home to check eligibility for residents 60 and older. They can arrange NYC Aging home care (bathing, dressing, laundry, shopping) and home delivered meals. Case managers do not charge, though some services carry an income-based fee or suggested contribution, and people on Medicaid get home care through Medicaid instead. Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469.

services.name: Older adult centers
services.desc: Free membership for New Yorkers 60 and older, with healthy meals and staff who help members apply for Medicare, Medicaid, SCRIE and SNAP. Some centers also serve breakfast, dinner or grab-and-go meals.

services.name: Caregiver support
services.desc: NYC Aging funds information and referrals, long-term care planning, support groups, counseling, caregiver training, respite care and limited financial help through community groups. Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469.

services.name: HIICAP Medicare counseling
services.desc: Free, confidential help with Medicare Parts A, B, C and D, Medigap, EPIC, the Medicare Savings Program and Extra Help, in person or by phone. Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 to reach a counselor.

services.name: Medicaid home care through HRA
services.desc: HRA's Home Care Services Program oversees Medicaid-funded home care, and managed long term care plans also cover home care for people who qualify. HRA's list of Home Care CASA offices shows CASA South, 2400 Fulton Street, 3rd Floor, Brooklyn (718-250-5631), under Brooklyn and Queens. To learn how to apply, call the DSS OneNumber at 718-557-1399.

services.name: Access-A-Ride and reduced fare
services.desc: Access-A-Ride (877-337-2017) is the MTA's shared-ride service, running 24 hours a day, for people whose disability keeps them from using buses and subways. Riders 65 and older pay a $1.50 reduced fare on subways and local buses, and OMNY reduced-fare questions go to 877-789-6669.

services.name: HEAP and SNAP
services.desc: HEAP helps low-income households pay for heat, and a household member 60 or older counts toward the benefit. Apply for HEAP or SNAP through ACCESS HRA, or call the DSS OneNumber at 718-557-1399 to have a HEAP application mailed.

services.name: SCRIE and SCHE
services.desc: SCRIE freezes the rent for tenants 62 and older in rent regulated apartments who spend over a third of their income on rent and whose household income is under the city's limit. Ask the Rent Freeze Hotline at 929-252-7242 for the current income limit. SCHE cuts the assessed value of a home owned by people 65 and older with income up to $58,399, and the deadline to apply or renew is March 15. Call 311 for either.

services.name: Elder abuse, crime and legal help
services.desc: NYC Aging's Elder Justice programs offer crisis help, safety planning and court help, C-PASS helps older adults hurt by scams, theft or assault, and Legal Assistance gives free legal help to residents 60 and older. Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469. For an adult at risk who cannot protect themselves, call the HRA Adult Protective Services Brooklyn office at 718-722-4812.

howto:
If your mom or dad lives in Brooklyn, start with Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 or the Brooklyn NY Connects office at PSS, 718-671-6200. Both are free, and you can call on your parent's behalf from New Jersey or anywhere else.

  1. Write down what is hard. Note your parent's age, address, income, Medicare and Medicaid status, and the tasks that have become hard, like stairs, bathing, cooking or getting to the doctor. Intake goes faster with this in hand.
  2. Ask for case management. A local agency does a phone intake, then a case manager visits the home. For residents 60 and older not on Medicaid, that can mean NYC Aging home care and home delivered meals, with fees based on income. Our home care guide explains the options.
  3. Go through HRA if Medicaid fits. Apply through ACCESS HRA or call the HRA Medicaid Helpline at 1-888-692-6116. To request a first assessment for personal care, CDPAP or a managed long term care plan, call the New York Independent Assessor at 855-222-8350. HRA lists its Home Care CASA office for Brooklyn and Queens, CASA South, at 2400 Fulton Street, 718-250-5631. See Medicaid for older New Yorkers and our CDPAP guide.
  4. Lower the monthly bills. Ask HIICAP, through Aging Connect, about the Medicare Savings Program and EPIC. A renter 62 or older may qualify for SCRIE, and a homeowner 65 or older for the SCHE exemption by March 15.
  5. Get the papers signed while your parent can. A power of attorney and a health care proxy let you act when your parent cannot. NYC Aging's Legal Assistance program is free for residents 60 and older. Read power of attorney in New York and health care proxy and MOLST.

If you think your parent is being harmed, neglected or exploited, call the Brooklyn APS office, at 718-722-4812, or the DSS OneNumber at 718-557-1399, weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Anyone can make a referral. When a person is eligible, APS visits within three business days, or within 24 hours if life is at risk. Call 911 if there is danger now, and see our APS guide.

faq.q: How do I get home care for my mom in Brooklyn?
faq.a: Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 or Brooklyn NY Connects at PSS, 718-671-6200, and ask for case management. A case manager will visit and can arrange NYC Aging home care if she is 60 or older and not on Medicaid. If she has Medicaid or may qualify, apply through HRA at 1-888-692-6116, and call the New York Independent Assessor at 855-222-8350 to request a first assessment.

faq.q: Who runs NY Connects in Brooklyn?
faq.a: PSS runs NY Connects in Brooklyn under contract with NYC Aging. Call 718-671-6200 for free, unbiased help with long-term care, benefits applications and home care referrals.

faq.q: Where is the HRA home care office for Brooklyn?
faq.a: HRA's list of Home Care CASA offices shows CASA South at 2400 Fulton Street, 3rd Floor, Brooklyn, 718-250-5631, under Brooklyn and Queens. To learn how to apply for Medicaid home care, call the DSS OneNumber at 718-557-1399.

faq.q: Can my dad get his rent frozen in Brooklyn?
faq.a: He may, through SCRIE, if he is 62 or older, named on the lease of a rent regulated apartment, spends more than a third of his income on rent and has household income under the city's limit. The NYC Department of Finance runs it. Call the Rent Freeze Hotline at 929-252-7242 for the current income limit, or call 311. First-time applicants can apply online through the Department of Finance.

faq.q: How much is the MTA senior fare in Brooklyn?
faq.a: Riders 65 and older pay $1.50 on subways and local, limited and Select Bus Service buses. Express buses cost $3.60 outside weekday rush hours. The online application is not available now, so apply in person at a Customer Service Center or by mail.

faq.q: Who do I call if I think my mother is being neglected in Brooklyn?
faq.a: Call the Brooklyn Adult Protective Services office, at 718-722-4812, or the DSS OneNumber at 718-557-1399, weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. For scams or theft, Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 connects you to NYC Aging's C-PASS program. If she is in danger right now, call 911.

howto:
Start with the Dutchess County Office for the Aging in Poughkeepsie, 845-486-2555 or toll free 866-486-2555. For broader questions about long-term care, the Dutchess NY Connects line is 845-475-3511. You can call for your parent from New Jersey or anywhere else.

  1. Ask for a case manager. Case managers and public health nurses can assess your parent at home, in the hospital or in a nursing home. Ask about the EISEP In Home Services Program for homemaking, personal care and respite. Our EISEP guide explains how it works.
  2. Line up meals and rides. Home delivered meals go to homebound adults 60 and older. For doctor visits, ask about GoGo Grandparent rides, or call Dutchess County Public Transit at 845-473-8424 about Dial-A-Ride and ADA paratransit.
  3. Check Medicaid home care. Adults 65 and older apply for Medicaid, including community based long term care and immediate need personal care, through the Department of Community and Family Services, main number 845-486-3000. To schedule a first assessment for Medicaid home care, your parent, or an authorized representative already on file, can call the New York Independent Assessor at 1-855-222-8350. Read Medicaid for older New Yorkers and our CDPAP guide.
  4. Get the legal papers signed. The Office for the Aging offers legal services to residents 60 and over. Make sure a health care proxy and power of attorney are signed while your parent can still decide. See power of attorney in New York.

If you suspect abuse, neglect or money being taken, call Dutchess County Adult Protective Services at 845-486-3300. The department is open weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The state Bureau of Adult Services helpline is 1-844-697-3505. Call 911 if someone is in danger now. Our APS guide covers what to expect.

faq.q: How do I get home care for my mom in Dutchess County?
faq.a: Call the Office for the Aging at 845-486-2555 and ask for a case manager. A case manager or public health nurse can assess her at home, in the hospital or in a nursing home and look at EISEP help such as personal care and homemaking. If she needs Medicaid home care, apply through the Department of Community and Family Services, main number 845-486-3000.

faq.q: Does Dutchess County deliver meals to homebound seniors?
faq.a: Yes. The Office for the Aging delivers meals to homebound adults 60 and older, one to five weekdays. Call 845-486-2555 or 866-486-2555.

faq.q: How can my dad get rides to medical appointments in Dutchess County?
faq.a: If he is not on Medicaid, ask the Office for the Aging (845-486-2555) about limited free GoGo Grandparent rides to non-emergency medical appointments. howto:
If your parent lives in Manhattan, one call to Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 gets things moving. You can also reach the Manhattan NY Connects office at Hudson Guild, 212-966-9852. Calling from New Jersey is fine.

  1. Request a case management intake. A local case management agency will ask questions by phone, then send a case manager to your parent's home. That visit decides what help your parent can get.
  2. Know the two tracks. If your parent is 60 or older and not on Medicaid, NYC Aging can fund home care for bathing, dressing, laundry and shopping, plus home delivered meals, with fees based on income. If your parent has Medicaid, home care comes through HRA instead.
  3. Start Medicaid home care with HRA. Call the HRA Medicaid Helpline at 1-888-692-6116 to apply, or the DSS OneNumber at 718-557-1399 for the Home Care Services Program. For a first assessment for personal care, CDPAP or managed long term care, call the New York Independent Assessor at 1-855-222-8350. Read Medicaid for older New Yorkers and our CDPAP guide.
  4. Book Medicare help. HIICAP counselors give free, confidential help with plans, Medigap and EPIC. Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 to reach one. See EPIC for prescriptions.
  5. Plan for transport. NYC Aging partners give rides to medical visits for people 60 and older who cannot use transit. Access-A-Ride (877-337-2017) is the MTA option for riders with a disability.
  6. Line up the legal papers. Free help is available to residents 60 and older through Legal Assistance to Older New Yorkers. See power of attorney in New York.

If you suspect abuse, neglect or money being taken, call HRA Adult Protective Services. Manhattan has two offices, North at 212-331-3458 and South at 212-331-3524, or use the DSS OneNumber, 718-557-1399. Call 911 if there is danger now. Our APS guide explains what happens next.

faq.q: How do I get help at home for my dad in Manhattan?
faq.a: Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 and ask for a case management intake. A case manager will visit his home and arrange services such as NYC Aging home care and home delivered meals if he is 60 or older and not on Medicaid. If he has Medicaid, call HRA at 718-557-1399 about the Home Care Services Program.

faq.q: Who runs NY Connects in Manhattan?
faq.a: Hudson Guild runs NY Connects in Manhattan under contract with NYC Aging. Call 212-966-9852, weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. and until 7 p.m. on Wednesdays.

faq.q: How do I apply for Medicaid home care for my mother in Manhattan?
faq.a: Call the HRA Medicaid Helpline at 1-888-692-6116 or apply online through ACCESS HRA. Once she has Medicaid, the first assessment for personal care, CDPAP or a managed long term care plan is scheduled through the New York Independent Assessor at 1-855-222-8350.

faq.q: Where can my parents get free Medicare counseling in Manhattan?
faq.a: NYC Aging's HIICAP counselors give free, confidential help with Medicare, Medigap, EPIC, the Medicare Savings Program and Extra Help. Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 to reach a counselor in person or by phone.

faq.q: Is there respite for family caregivers in Manhattan?
faq.a: Yes. NYC Aging works with community partners to offer respite care along with counseling, support groups and caregiver training. NYC Aging funded social adult day care can also give caregivers a break. Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469.

faq.q: Who do I call about elder abuse in Manhattan?
faq.a: Call HRA Adult Protective Services at the Manhattan North office (212-331-3458) or Manhattan South office (212-331-3524), or the DSS OneNumber at 718-557-1399. For scams and crimes, Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 connects you to NYC Aging's C-PASS program. In an emergency, call 911.

howto:
The first call is NY Connects at the Nassau County Office for the Aging in Uniondale, 516-227-8900. You can call on your parent's behalf, and the same number covers in-home services, meals and caregiver help.

  1. Explain what changed. Give your parent's age, town, insurance and what is hard now, such as bathing, cooking or getting home from the hospital.
  2. Ask for an EISEP assessment if your parent is 60 or older and not on Medicaid. A care coordinator assesses your parent, writes a care plan and monitors it. Our EISEP guide explains how the program works.
  3. Set up meals and rides. Ask if your parent qualifies for home delivered meals, which a case manager decides in a home visit. For trips, NICE Able-Ride (516-228-4000) serves people whose disability keeps them off regular buses.
  4. Check Medicaid home care. If your parent has or may get Medicaid, call DSS Medical Services at 516-227-8111 or Medicaid at 516-227-8000. Approval needs a nursing assessment. Read Medicaid for older New Yorkers and our CDPAP guide.
  5. Get the legal papers in order. The Senior Citizen Law Project (516-292-8088) helps with wills, powers of attorney, health care proxies and Medicaid planning. See power of attorney in New York and health care proxies and MOLST.

If you think an adult is being abused, neglected or exploited, call Nassau County Adult Protective Services at 516-227-8395, the number on the county Adult Services page. APS services may be provided free, without regard to income. Nights, weekends and holidays, call the DSS after-hours line at 516-573-8626. Call 911 if someone is in danger now. howto:
In Orange County, most doors open through one number, NY Connects at 845-615-3710. It handles referrals for EISEP in-home help, home delivered meals, legal help and HEAP, so you rarely need to hunt for separate offices.

  1. Call NY Connects and explain what changed. Share your parent's age, town, income, insurance and what daily tasks have become hard. If your parent is homebound, ask about a home visit from an Aging Services Specialist (845-615-3700).
  2. Ask for an EISEP referral if your parent is 60 or older and not on Medicaid. A case manager visits the home, writes a service plan and arranges help. Costs depend on income, and people below a state-set level pay nothing. Our EISEP guide has the details.
  3. Ask about meals. NY Connects takes referrals for home delivered meals. If your parent still gets out, a senior dining site serves meals for a suggested contribution of $3.50, with a reservation 24 hours ahead.
  4. Check Medicaid home care if needs are bigger. Call Orange County DSS at 845-291-4000 about Medicaid. To schedule a first assessment for personal care, CDPAP or a managed long term care plan, call the New York Independent Assessor at 1-855-222-8350. Read Medicaid for older New Yorkers and our CDPAP guide.
  5. Get the paperwork done. The county's contract elder law attorney can help residents 60 and older with simple wills, health care proxies and powers of attorney. Ask NY Connects for a referral, and see health care proxy and MOLST.
  6. Look after yourself. The Caregiver Resource Center (845-862-5333) offers counseling, support groups and respite. You qualify if you are 18 or older and caring for someone 60 or older.

If you think your parent is being abused, neglected or exploited, call the Orange County Adult Protective Services unit at 845-291-2800. If your parent is in immediate danger, call 911. Our APS guide explains what happens next.

howto:
Start with the Putnam County Office for Senior Resources in Carmel, 845-808-1700. The same number reaches Putnam NY Connects, EISEP, meals, HIICAP and legal help, and you can call for your parent from New Jersey or anywhere else.

  1. Ask for an assessment. Explain what has changed, such as a fall, a hospital stay or trouble with bathing. For EISEP, a case manager assesses your parent first, and the cost is shared based on income. Our EISEP guide explains how it works.
  2. Line up meals and rides. Home delivered meals need a physician referral and a home assessment. For doctor visits, ask about volunteer medical transportation at extension 47104.
  3. Check Medicaid home care. If your parent may qualify for Medicaid, call the Department of Social Services Medicaid unit at 845-808-1500, extension 45263.   4. Get the legal papers signed. The office arranges consultations on wills, health care proxies and powers of attorney by appointment. See power of attorney in New York and health care proxy and MOLST.
  5. Look after the caregiver. The Caregiver Program (extension 47113) offers counseling, support groups and workshops. See caregiver support in New York.

If you suspect abuse, neglect or money being taken, call Putnam County Adult Protective Services at 845-808-1500, extension 45262, during business hours. howto:
Start with one call to NY Connects at the Rockland County Office for the Aging, 845-364-3444. You can call from New Jersey or anywhere else. Staff will do a short phone review of your parent's needs and tell you which programs fit.

  2. Ask about EISEP. If your parent is 60 or older and not on Medicaid, ask for an EISEP referral. A case manager looks at what help is needed at home, and costs depend on income. Our EISEP guide explains the sliding scale.
  3. Ask about meals and rides. Home delivered meals are for residents who are homebound and cannot shop or cook. TRIPS paratransit (845-364-8747) gives rides to residents 60 and older who cannot use regular county buses.
  4. Look at Medicaid if money is tight or care needs are high. Medicaid covers home care for people with medical documentation of need. For a first assessment for personal care, CDPAP or a managed long term care plan, call the New York Independent Assessor at 1-855-222-8350. See Medicaid for older New Yorkers.

services.name: Legal help
services.desc: The Nassau/Suffolk Law Services Senior Citizen Law Project (516-292-8088) gives free civil legal help to low-income people in both counties. Touro Law Center's Senior Citizens' Law Program (631-761-7062) offers free legal advice and education for older adults and their families.

services.name: Medicaid home care (DSS)
services.desc: The DSS Home Care Intake Unit handles personal care and CDPAP for people on Medicaid who are not enrolled in Medicaid Managed Care, at 631-854-9585. For questions on an open Medicaid case, call Medicaid East in Riverhead (631-852-3570) or Medicaid West in Smithtown (631-853-8408).

services.name: HEAP heating help
services.desc: People 60 and older, or living with a disability, apply for HEAP through the Office for the Aging at 631-853-8326 during the HEAP season (under 60, call 631-853-8820). For heating emergencies after 4:30 p.m. and on weekends, call 631-854-9100.

howto:
Start with NY Connects at the Suffolk County Office for the Aging in Hauppauge, 631-853-8200, weekdays 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. It covers the whole county, from Huntington and Babylon to the North and South Forks, and you can call for a parent who lives there.

  1. Ask for an EISEP home visit early. A case manager comes to the home, looks at what your parent can and cannot do, and writes a care plan. There is a waiting list, so get on it soon. Our EISEP guide explains the program.
  2. Set up meals. Call the nutrition line at 631-853-8227 about home delivered meals or a group meal site near your parent.
  3. Sort out rides. If a disability keeps your parent off regular buses, apply for SCAT through the Office for People with Disabilities at 631-853-8333. Once approved, book trips at 631-738-1150 from 1 to 5 days ahead. Town senior rides are another option for local trips, and medical appointments have priority.
  4. Check Medicaid home care. If your parent has Medicaid and is not in a managed care plan, call the DSS Home Care Intake Unit at 631-854-9585 for personal care or CDPAP. If your parent has Medicare and Medicaid, New York Medicaid Choice (1-888-401-6582) explains the home care plans. Read Medicaid for older New Yorkers and our CDPAP guide.
  5. Put the legal papers in place. A health care proxy and power of attorney should be signed while your parent can still decide. See power of attorney in New York and health care proxies and MOLST.

If you suspect abuse, neglect or exploitation, call Suffolk County Adult Protective Services at 631-854-3232. The state courts' elder justice directory also lists a 24 hour APS hotline, 631-854-9100. Calls are confidential and may be anonymous. Call 911 if someone is in immediate danger. Our APS guide covers what to expect.

faq.q: How do I get home care for my dad in Suffolk County?
faq.a: Call NY Connects at the Office for the Aging, 631-853-8200, and ask about EISEP. A case manager visits, assesses his needs and writes a care plan, but there is a waiting list. If he has Medicaid and is not in a managed care plan, call the DSS Home Care Intake Unit at 631-854-9585.

faq.q: Can my mom get meals delivered in Suffolk County?
faq.a: Yes, through the nutrition program that serves her area, and there are also congregate meal sites with a hot meal and company. Call the Office for the Aging nutrition line at 631-853-8227 to find the program near her.

faq.q: How does SCAT work in Suffolk County?
faq.a: SCAT is curb to curb paratransit for people who meet federal ADA paratransit rules. Apply through the Office for People with Disabilities at 631-853-8333, and you hear back within 21 days. Rides cost $4.00 per trip, exact change, and are booked at 631-738-1150 from 1 to 5 days ahead.

faq.q: Where can my parents get Medicare help in Suffolk County?
faq.a: HIICAP counselors answer Medicare and health insurance questions at 631-979-9490, extension 18. Office for the Aging Senior Advocates also visit over 50 sites around the county to help, and the schedule is on the Office for the Aging calendar.

faq.q: Can I get paid to care for my parent in Suffolk County?
faq.a: Possibly, through CDPAP, a Medicaid program that lets your parent choose their own caregiver. If your parent has Medicaid and is not enrolled in Medicaid Managed Care, call the DSS Home Care Intake Unit at 631-854-9585. If your parent is in a plan, call the plan.

faq.q: Who do I call if I think my mother is being abused in Suffolk County?
faq.a: Call Suffolk County Adult Protective Services at 631-854-3232. The state courts' elder justice directory also lists a 24 hour APS hotline at 631-854-9100. If she is in immediate danger, call 911.

howto:
Start with the Sullivan County Office for the Aging in Monticello, 845-807-0241, weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. For questions about long-term care choices, Sullivan NY Connects is at 845-807-0257. You can call for your parent from New Jersey, Pennsylvania or anywhere else.

  1. Ask for EISEP case management. If your parent is 60 or older and not on Medicaid, a case manager works with you to figure out what help is needed and arranges it on a sliding fee. On the main line, EISEP case management is option 3. Our EISEP guide explains the fee.
  2. Line up meals and rides. Reserve a lunch at a dining site at 845-807-0254, or ask about homebound meals. Once your parent registers with the office, the Shopping Bus (845-807-0244) runs door to door to Monticello stores.
  3. Check Medicaid home care. If your parent has Medicaid, the Department of Social Services Personal Care unit (845-292-0100) arranges home care after a doctor sends a medical recommendation. To schedule a first assessment for Medicaid home care, your parent, or an authorized representative already on file, can call the New York Independent Assessor at 1-855-222-8350. Start with Medicaid for older New Yorkers and our CDPAP guide.
  4. Get the papers in order. The office's contract attorney can help with health care proxies and living wills. See health care proxy and MOLST and power of attorney in New York.

If you suspect abuse, neglect or money being taken, call the Sullivan County Adult Protective Services intake line at 845-513-2390. The Department of Social Services in Liberty is open weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Call 911 if someone is in danger now. Our APS guide covers what to expect.

faq.q: How do I get home care for my dad in Sullivan County?
faq.a: If he is 60 or older and not on Medicaid, call the Office for the Aging at 845-807-0241 and ask about EISEP. A case manager helps decide what he needs, and the cost is on a sliding fee scale. If he has Medicaid, the Department of Social Services Personal Care unit coordinates home care. Call 845-292-0100.

faq.q: Does Sullivan County deliver meals to seniors?
faq.a: The Senior Nutrition Program serves homebound meals as well as lunches at five dining sites. Dining site reservations are needed at least 24 hours ahead at 845-807-0254. The suggested contribution for people over 60 is $3, and no one is denied a meal for not giving.

faq.q: How can my mom get to the store in Sullivan County without driving?
faq.a: The county Shopping Buses give door-to-door rides to stores in Monticello, with a set day for each town. She needs to be 60 or older and registered with the Office for the Aging. Call 845-807-0244 ahead to reserve.

faq.q: What does EISEP cost in Sullivan County?
faq.a: The cost is based on a sliding fee scale set by income and housing expenses. EISEP is for adults 60 and older who are not receiving Medicaid. Call 845-807-0241 to ask what your parent would pay.

faq.q: Where can seniors get legal help in Sullivan County?
faq.a: The Office for the Aging provides legal services through a contract with a Sullivan County attorney. Help covers Social Security and Medicare problems, landlord and tenant issues, public benefit appeals, and health care proxies and living wills. Call 845-807-0241.

faq.q: Who do I report elder abuse to in Sullivan County?
faq.a: Call the Adult Protective Services intake line at 845-513-2390. If someone is in danger right now, call 911.

services.name: Elder abuse and crime help

howto:
For a parent in the Bronx, start with Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 or the Bronx NY Connects office at Neighborhood SHOPP, 347-862-5200. Both are free, and you can call for your parent from New Jersey.

  1. Ask for case management. Explain what your parent needs help with, such as bathing, shopping or meals. A local case management agency does a phone intake, then a case manager visits the apartment to check eligibility and set up services.
  2. Ask what your parent can get without Medicaid. Residents 60 and older who are not on Medicaid may get NYC Aging home care, home delivered meals and help applying for benefits. Fees depend on income.
  3. If your parent has Medicaid or may qualify, go through HRA. HRA's Home Care Services Program oversees Medicaid-funded home care in New York City, and managed long term care plans also cover home care for people who qualify. Call the DSS OneNumber at 718-557-1399 or the HRA Medicaid Helpline at 1-888-692-6116. A first assessment for personal care, CDPAP or a managed long term care plan is scheduled through the New York Independent Assessor, 1-855-222-8350. See Medicaid for older New Yorkers.
  4. Think about CDPAP. It lets your parent hire their own aide, and an adult child can be hired. A spouse cannot. Our CDPAP guide walks through it.
  5. Sort out rides. NYC Aging partners drive older adults to medical appointments. For a parent with a disability, Access-A-Ride (877-337-2017) covers the whole city. Read our Access-A-Ride guide.
  6. Get help for yourself. NYC Aging's caregiver programs offer counseling, support groups, training and respite. See caregiver support in New York.

If you think your parent is being harmed, neglected or exploited, call the Bronx APS office at 929-252-8500 or the DSS OneNumber, 718-557-1399, weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. When eligible, APS visits within three business days, or within 24 hours if the situation is life-threatening. In an emergency, call 911. Our APS guide explains the process.

faq.q: How do I get home care for my mom in the Bronx?
faq.a: Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 and ask for case management. A local agency will do a phone intake and send a case manager to her home to set up help, including NYC Aging home care if she is not on Medicaid. If she has Medicaid, call HRA's DSS OneNumber at 718-557-1399 about the Home Care Services Program.

faq.q: Where is the NY Connects office for the Bronx?
faq.a: Neighborhood SHOPP runs NY Connects in the Bronx for NYC Aging. Call 347-862-5200, weekdays 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., with hours until 7 p.m. on Wednesdays.

faq.q: Can my dad get rides to doctor appointments in the Bronx?
faq.a: Yes. NYC Aging partners give rides to medical appointments for residents 60 and older who lack transportation or cannot use public transit. Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469. If he has a disability, he can also apply for Access-A-Ride.

faq.q: How do I get meals delivered to my parent in the Bronx?
faq.a: Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469. Home delivered meals are arranged through a local case management agency, which checks eligibility during a home visit.

faq.q: Is there free legal help for seniors in the Bronx?
faq.a: Yes. NYC Aging's Legal Assistance to Older New Yorkers program gives free legal help to residents 60 and older, including housing, guardianship, consumer fraud and public benefits cases. Call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 to be matched with a provider.

faq.q: Who do I call if my mother is being scammed or abused in the Bronx?
faq.a: For a scam or crime, call Aging Connect at 212-244-6469 to reach NYC Aging's C-PASS program. If she cannot protect herself, call the Bronx APS office at 929-252-8500 or HRA's DSS OneNumber at 718-557-1399. If she is in danger right now, call 911.

services.desc: For people 60 and older who need help with eating, dressing, bathing or toileting that family cannot fully cover. A case manager visits at home, builds a care plan and arranges housekeepers or homemakers, with fees on a sliding scale. Call 914-813-6442.

services.name: Respite and emergency response systems
services.desc: Through EISEP, clients can also get respite care and extra services such as emergency response systems and other needed equipment.

services.name: Congregate meals
services.desc: Meals for adults 60 and older are served five or more days a week at approved nutrition sites and multi-purpose centers across the county. Pre-registration is required, and giving a contribution is voluntary.

services.name: Home delivered meals
services.desc: Meals brought to medically eligible homebound seniors who cannot get to a dining site. Local nutrition sites run the deliveries, and pre-registration is required.

services.name: Caregiver coaching
services.desc: Through the Livable Communities Caregiver Coaching program, trained volunteer coaches give family caregivers one-on-one support, so they can understand their options and make informed decisions about care for an older or disabled loved one.

services.name: Medicare information line and workshops
services.desc: The department holds free sessions that explain Medicare insurance options. Register through the Medicare Information Line at 914-813-6100.

services.name: Project Lifesaver
services.desc: A free program for families of people with Alzheimer's disease or another dementia who may wander. The person wears a bracelet that county police can track by radio signal. Westchester Jewish Community Services runs it, at 914-761-0600, extension 2230.

services.name: Medicaid home care (DSS)
services.desc: Medicaid can help pay for personal care, home health aides and CDPAP for people who are medically and financially eligible. If your parent has Medicaid but is not in a managed care plan, call the DSS Home Care Unit at 914-813-6612. For Medicaid applications, call 914-813-6147. People in a Medicaid managed care plan should call their plan.

services.name: HEAP heating help (DSS)
services.desc: HEAP helps income-eligible households pay for heat, and having someone 60 or older in the home counts toward eligibility and benefits. Apply online at myBenefits.ny.gov, in person at a DSS district office, or on a paper application. Questions go to 914-995-3333.

howto:
The fastest start is NY Connects at the Westchester County Department of Senior Programs and Services, 914-813-6300. Calls are confidential, and you can call on your parent's behalf from New Jersey or anywhere else.

  1. Describe the need plainly. Tell the specialist your parent's age, town, insurance and what has changed, such as a fall, a hospital stay or trouble with bathing and meals.
  2. Ask for an EISEP home visit if your parent is 60 or older. The case management unit (914-813-6442) sends a case manager to the home for a face-to-face assessment. They build a care plan with your parent and family and reassess at least every six months. The home visit is free, and in-home help is on a sliding fee. Our EISEP guide explains how the fee works.
  3. Line up meals and rides. Ask about home delivered meals if your parent is homebound. For trips, Bee-Line ParaTransit (914-995-7272) gives shared rides to people who cannot use regular buses.
  4. Check Medicaid home care. If your parent has Medicaid and is not in a managed care plan, call the DSS Home Care Unit at 914-813-6612. If your parent is not on Medicaid yet, call 914-813-6147 about applying. Medicaid can cover personal care, CDPAP and managed long term care plans. To schedule a first assessment, call the New York Independent Assessor at 1-855-222-8350. Start with Medicaid for older New Yorkers and our CDPAP guide.
  5. Plan for the long run. Make sure a health care proxy and power of attorney are signed while your parent can still decide. See power of attorney in New York.

If you suspect abuse, neglect or money being taken, call Westchester Adult Protective Services intake at 914-995-2259, weekdays 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Evenings, weekends and holidays, call DSS emergency services at 914-995-2099. The Department of Senior Programs and Services also runs an Elder Abuse Help Line at 914-813-6436. Call 911 if someone is in danger now. Our APS guide covers what to expect.

faq.q: How do I get home care for my mom in Westchester County?
faq.a: Call NY Connects at 914-813-6300 or the EISEP case management unit at 914-813-6442 if she is 60 or older. A case manager visits her at home, builds a care plan and arranges help on a sliding fee. If she has Medicaid and is not in a managed care plan, the DSS Home Care Unit (914-813-6612) handles Medicaid home care.

faq.q: Does Westchester County deliver meals to homebound seniors?
faq.a: Yes. Home delivered meals go to medically eligible homebound seniors 60 and older who cannot get to a dining site. Local nutrition sites run the deliveries, and pre-registration is required.

faq.q: How can my dad get rides to the doctor in Westchester?
faq.a: Bee-Line ParaTransit gives shared curb to curb rides if a disability keeps him from using regular Bee-Line buses. Call 914-995-7272 and press 3 to ask for an application. Each trip costs $5.

faq.q: Can I get paid to care for my parent in Westchester County?
faq.a: Possibly, through CDPAP, a Medicaid program that lets your parent choose and hire their own caregiver. A friend or relative can be hired, but a spouse or designated representative cannot. If your parent has Medicaid and is not in a managed care plan, call the DSS Home Care Unit at 914-813-6612 to ask how to start. If your parent is in a plan, call the plan.

faq.q: Where can my parents learn about Medicare in Westchester?
faq.a: The Department of Senior Programs and Services runs free sessions that explain Medicare insurance options. Register through the Medicare Information Line at 914-813-6100.

faq.q: Who do I call if I think my father is being neglected in Westchester?
faq.a: Call Westchester Adult Protective Services intake at 914-995-2259, weekdays 9 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. After hours, on weekends and holidays, call DSS emergency services at 914-995-2099. If he is in danger right now, call 911.
